title: Renamings, transplants and flips in place
claim: Over abstract names, with count laws of degree four: (L1) in a world of finite components a finite change is a renaming exactly when it keeps the multiset of types of the components it touches, so a change of values on one copy of (B, c) is a renaming exactly when the new colouring is an automorphic image of c; (L2) on four-regular trees no change of values alone is a renaming; (L3) the switch flips a neighbour distinction in place, in two copies of a finite component (edge on a cycle) and in tree worlds (a partner edge closing a cycle exists in every cover); (L4) transplants: a place can be moved by a finite rewiring that is not a renaming, so excluding renamings alone is not enough and flips are counted in place; (L5) where no allowed state has a mixed edge, and in law 48, no finite change of values flips a value in a world of infinite components; (L6, after the census) least fixed points decide finite value flips in a cover, for one place in some tree world, and for both ends of an edge in some tree world. Checks: all 90 board-value knots native in place in some world of finite pieces (84 frozen witnesses, 6 by hand); on trees 26 native in place in some tree world and 64 in none, 58 laws with no value flippable at all. Read by an independent referee.
failure_conditions: A finite change that keeps the type multiset of the components it touches and is not a renaming, or the converse (against L1).
A nontrivial renaming of an infinite tree world that changes no neighbour distinction (against L2).
A switch on a cycle of a finite component, or in a tree world, that is a renaming or not minimal (against L3).
A finite change of values alone that flips a value in a tree world of a cascading law (against L5).
foundation_claim_scope: Boards made of neighbour distinctions on a countably infinite set of names with no letters; count laws; the source-aware reading counted up to renaming as defined in the pre-registration. No change to the canonical knot test.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the coordinator's go-ahead on 2026-11-10; read before publication by an independent referee (a fresh Claude agent given only the proof), whose suggested joint recursion was then run.
validation.status: proved by hand; finite checks in check.py passed (result.json); read before publication by an independent referee, L1 to L6 sound, fixes made
validation.novelty: Elementary consequences of standard facts (covering graphs, least fixed points, the 2-switch); folklore risk high.
